These conditions align with typical mid-May climatology for the region, where humidity and precipitation often moderate temperatures below the seasonal average near 31°C. Trader-implied probabilities reflect this outlook, with 28°C holding the plurality at 35 percent amid lingering uncertainty in exact timing of any brief clearing that could push readings to 30°C or higher. eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from European and global models point to a highest temperature in Istanbul on May 21 likely falling between 19°C and 21°C, driven by a passing frontal system that brings increased cloud cover and scattered showers over the Bosphorus region. These conditions limit surface heating compared to typical late-May climatology, where daily maxima average near 22°C, while the moderating influence of the adjacent Sea of Marmara and variable wind patterns introduce further uncertainty in peak readings. Key variables include the exact timing of any clearing skies, which could allow brief warming to 22°C or higher, versus persistent overcast that caps values at 18°C or below; model consensus remains split, with resolution hinging on official meteorological service observations at the end of the day.
